chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jumhoor al-A'mi narrated from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jumhoor, from his father, from Sulayman ibn Sama'a, from Abul Jarood, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) that he said:

When the Qa'im appears in Mecca, his caller will announce that no one is to carry with him food or drink. He will carry with him the rock of Moses ibn 'Izran, which is the burden of a camel. Whenever they stop to rest, springs will well up from it. Whoever is hungry will be satisfied, and whoever is thirsty will be quenched, and their beasts will be quenched until they descend to Najaf from the rear of Kufa.

key_terms.النَّجَفُ: Najaf, a city near Kufa where the Imam's forces will gather
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the Awaited Imam in Shia eschatology
key_terms.الْكُوفَةُ: Kufa, a major city in Iraq associated with the Imam's movement
key_terms.حَجَرَ مُوسَى: The rock of Moses, a miraculous object carried by the Imam

ai.seo_question: What are the miraculous signs and provisions of al-Qa'im during his emergence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* details the miraculous sustenance accompanying al-Qa'im’s journey from Mecca to Najaf, emphasizing the divine provision that renders carrying provisions unnecessary. The reference to the 'rock of Moses' (Hajar Musa) alludes to the Quranic miracle of water springing from stone, linking the Imam’s emergence to the legacy of the Prophets. This event underscores the concept of *ghaybat al-kubra* preparations, where the Imam’s physical presence brings immediate relief and spiritual renewal to his followers.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (29) Muhammad bin Hammam and Muhammad bin al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Jumhoor narrated from al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Jumhoor from his father from Sulayman bin Suma’a from Abul Jarood that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said:

“When al-Qa’im appears in Mecca, his caller will announce that no one is to carry with him food or drink. He (al-Qa’im) will carry with him the rock of Prophet Moses, which is as a burden of a camel. Whenever they stop to rest, the rock will well. Hungry and thirsty ones will eat and drink and feed their cattle until they will reach Najaf, which is near Kufa.”
